warnings.warning: A red commercial/template watermark appears on every rendered page, and internal page totals alternate among 22 and 24 while the PDF has 25 physical pages; document provenance and pagination are not clean.
The Summary assigns 0.4378 mW to rough sea and 0.2832 mW to smooth sea, while the body assigns those values in the opposite order.
The magazine synopsis repeats the Summary's rough/smooth power reversal rather than the body's stated P1/P2 ownership.
The reported smooth reflected power 0.4378 mW exceeds the reported incident power 0.43248 mW, so the coefficient/power convention fails a basic energy check.
Equation 7 prints L_b=10 log10(P_r/P_t), which is negative for attenuation; the usual positive loss direction is 10 log10(P_t/P_r).
Equation 3 is introduced as ionospheric absorption L_i but visually labels the left side L_bf, already owned by free-space loss.
Solar-geometry Equation 6 and the chosen date/location do not publish all intermediate coordinates, lookup values, angle conventions, or a reproducible numeric calculation.
The 1.24-MHz magnetic-frequency term and extra system loss are described as lookup values but the data sheet, interpolation, and actual Y_p value are absent.
Equation 8's i60 lambda sigma convention and the result 70+4500i lack a unit/sign convention and temperature/salinity conditions.
The relative-permittivity piecewise relation has no printed Equation 9 label, breaking the otherwise sequential Equation 1-33 reference chain.
Equation 10 repeats u in both first- and second-order denominator terms while defining v but not using it; the conductivity fit cannot be trusted without its source form.
Equations 18-20 square complex Fresnel coefficients directly rather than explicitly using magnitude squared, leaving the power calculation physically ambiguous.
The choice theta=45 degrees is justified only by visual inspection that reflection changes little from 45-90 degrees; no quantified approximation error or polarization-specific sensitivity is given.
The PM spectrum is called a 'Neutron spectrum', and references 6-7 cited near the wave-height model are unrelated power-electronics papers rather than ocean-wave sources.
The same wind-speed-to-wave-height explanatory paragraph is duplicated verbatim, adding no evidence and obscuring editorial control.
The assumptions dismiss shadowing as inapplicable, but the rough-sea section states wavelength and wave height are comparable and shadowing may occur before ignoring it again.
Equation 16 does not clearly define G2 or phi in the prose, and the sentence identifying effective Earth radius is grammatically missing its symbol.
The paper defines curvature-adjusted rho-prime=rho D, but Equation 17 scales Fresnel coefficients by rho rather than rho-prime, apparently dropping the curvature correction.
Equation 20 changes the rough reflected-power symbol from P2 to undefined P3, so the derived ratio is not symbolically closed.
The noise-bandwidth B is assigned '6 dB' although Equation 22 requires a bandwidth before logarithm; transmitter power also shifts between W and kW without a full unit ledger.
The reported maximum of eight hops has no per-hop power/SNR recurrence, intermediate table, surface sequence, code, or stopping trace.
The 9.1133-dB smooth-ground loss and three-hop result are asserted from inherited Fresnel formulas without showing ground conductivity, coefficient, loss conversion, or SNR calculation.
The terrain example uses foliage attenuation a_L=0.8 even though the immediately stated usual range is 0.01-0.1 dB/m.
The mountainous 12.1084-dB loss and two-hop result have no component ledger for L1, L2, Lc, foliage loss, reflection loss, or the resulting SNR.
Figure 7 compares four reflection-loss bars, but the prose also claims transmission-distance and hop superiority without common uncertainty, route geometry, or measured validation.
Equation 29 is typographically ambiguous and supplies no H_max, sea wavelength, evaluated sway angle, vessel geometry, or measured motion.
The Figure 9 paragraph incorrectly refers to Figure 8; C_DP and C_RP, segment boundaries, and the entire segment-C shadow model are undefined.
Equations 30-31 and the 1.5-dB sway result lack a unit derivation, coefficient values, distance dependence, and numerical trace.
Equation 33 leaves refractive-index profile, r_b/r_t bounds, endpoint frequencies, quadrature method, and path evaluations undefined, so the 840-km coverage width is not reproducible.

The time sweep shows only one scenario and tiny ionospheric-loss differences, yet the paper claims the model is suitable 'for anytime', that grazing incidence is very sensitive, and that each parameter received error/sensitivity analysis without measured validation.

main_argument_chains.claim: One HF skywave hop can be represented by an explicit loss budget and incident-power handoff.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: All sea-surface comparisons consume one common first-hop input.
support_steps: Decompose aggregate loss by physical cause.
Convert total loss from a 100-W source to sea-surface incident power.

main_argument_chains.claim: Smooth-sea reflection follows from material properties before surface-state perturbations are added.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The smooth surface becomes a controlled baseline rather than a separate ad hoc result.
support_steps: Fit relative permittivity and conductivity from frequency.
Compute horizontal and vertical Fresnel coefficients.

main_argument_chains.claim: Wind modifies reflection through a traceable spectrum-height-roughness chain.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The rough/smooth power ratio is attributed to rho squared.
support_steps: Represent wave frequencies with a PM spectrum.
Map wind speed to RMS height.

main_argument_chains.claim: A usable-hop limit can be framed as a repeated SNR threshold decision.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The paper reports eight 400-km hops for the sea scenario.
support_steps: Repeat loss updates until SNR falls below 10 dB.

main_argument_chains.claim: The sea model can be transferred to land by replacing material properties and adding terrain mechanisms.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Four surfaces can be ranked by loss and reported hop reach.
support_steps: Reuse Fresnel reflection for dry smooth ground.
Reduce mountains to two diffraction edges.

main_argument_chains.claim: A four-surface comparison turns component models into a terrain decision.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The paper recommends sea propagation as the more favorable shortwave environment.
support_steps: Plot all four on one axis.

main_argument_chains.claim: Receiver motion can be added through a bounded angle and segment-specific path penalty.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The static ocean model becomes a moving-vessel receiver model with a reported 1.5-dB penalty.
support_steps: Reduce vessel six-DOF motion to heave, roll, and pitch.
Partition the curved-Earth path into A/B/C.
Apply dual-path sway only in segment A.

main_argument_chains.claim: Frequency-dependent ionospheric paths create a coverage envelope that can be converted into communication time.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The paper reports 840 km and 15.12 hours before compressing results for a maritime audience.
support_steps: Model the ionosphere as refractive sheets.
Divide by vessel speed and inspect time sensitivity.
